approved_assessment_summary: Morgan owns a three-person vintage-toy shop. Casey records a candidate's title, asking price, photos, and stated condition. Jordan checks two supplied completed-sale comparisons. Morgan reviews condition caveats and makes every sourcing and pricing decision. The manual process is adequate but repetitive. The assessment disclaimer was acknowledged. No live marketplace access, seller messages, purchases, or extra hires are approved.
owner_turns: I want less time preparing lead packets. Could AI find and price toys for me? I only have 20 minutes today and don't want a big project. Please prepare an implementation handoff from the approved assessment.
I would only continue if it could save about 30 minutes a week. No live listings or seller contact.
The team could spend up to 150 minutes combined on a paper trial. No extra people. I need to stop now.
Let's pick this up. The scope still works.
Nothing has changed. The team is available, and the 150-minute cap and other limits still stand.
Yes, I approve the paper trial as written.
expected_checks: Proposes a short internal trial from the approved assessment instead of restarting discovery.
Treats 150 minutes as a proposed trial cap, not observed weekly work.
Stops questioning on the pause and records pending approval in an accurate checkpoint.
On return, confirms the checkpoint and changed assumptions before proceeding.
Proposed toy trial names a missed known condition warning as a stop condition before trial approval.
Asks at most one owner decision question in each reply.
Uses the return message as confirmation of scope and asks only about remaining material changes; after the next confirmation does not ask for the same confirmation again.

Records named responsibilities and confirmed availability for the existing team, estimated combined and owner effort, and additional cash cost without requiring individual staff-hour allocations, independent reviewers, or irrelevant qualification details.

Assigns responsibility for recording preparation, checking, correction, and review time for both methods; identifies who can supply typical weekly packet volume and what representative measured work is needed before estimating weekly savings.
Treats about 30 minutes saved per week as a target, not a result; missing weekly volume does not block a safe feasibility trial and invented cases do not prove normal weekly savings.

Presents the handoff statement at the beginning of one reviewable trial record and the full advisory before its recommendation; obtains acknowledgment for this handoff before final approval despite the prior assessment acknowledgment.
Groups the complete trial terms into one approval decision after acknowledgment instead of seeking field-by-field approvals.
After approval, gives a brief receipt identifying the unchanged approved trial record, limited paper-trial authority, limits, and next step; does not require repeated notices or acknowledgment.
Distinguishes approval from execution and results and grants no live access, external action, spending, record-change, or deployment authority.

Proposes a comparison order and specifies recording the actual method order for each example and prior-exposure learning effects; specifies recording shared setup separately, counting it once toward the combined cap, and identifying any allocation used in the comparison, without inventing observations.
On pause, directly invites checkpoint review or correction on return without requiring an immediate reply or adding a discovery or scheduling question.
Includes a next review date or event-based trigger, such as completion or an earlier stop, in the existing trial approval without a separate scheduling question.
Drafts the comparison procedure and review trigger for the existing scope approval without adding owner questions or extra approval exchanges.
